{{Short description|Type of supersymmetric quantum field theory}}
{{Distinguish| Wess–Zumino–Witten model}}

In [[theoretical physics]], the '''Wess–Zumino model''' has become the first known example of an interacting four-dimensional [[quantum field theory]] with linearly realised [[supersymmetry]]. In 1974, [[Julius Wess]] and [[Bruno Zumino]] studied, using modern terminology, dynamics of a single [[chiral superfield]] (composed of a complex [[scalar (physics)|scalar]] and a [[spinor]] [[fermion]]) whose cubic [[superpotential]] leads to a [[renormalizable]] theory.<ref name=wess-zumino>{{cite journal |first1=J. |last1=Wess |first2=B. |last2=Zumino |title=Supergauge transformations in four dimensions |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=70 |issue=1 |pages=39–50 |year=1974 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(74)90355-1 |bibcode=1974NuPhB..70...39W |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/201649 }}</ref> It is a special case of [[4D N = 1 global supersymmetry]].

The treatment in this article largely follows that of Figueroa-O'Farrill's lectures on supersymmetry,<ref name=BUSSTEPP>{{cite arXiv |first=J. M. |last=Figueroa-O'Farrill |title=Busstepp Lectures on Supersymmetry |year=2001 |eprint=hep-th/0109172 }}</ref> and to some extent of Tong.<ref name=tong>{{cite web |url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/susy.html |title=Lectures on Supersymmetry |last=Tong |first=David |website=Lectures on Theoretical Physics |access-date=July 19, 2022}}</ref>

The model is an important model in supersymmetric quantum field theory. It is arguably the simplest supersymmetric field theory in four dimensions, and is ungauged.

== The Wess–Zumino action ==

=== Preliminary treatment ===

==== Spacetime and matter content ====

In a preliminary treatment, the theory is defined on flat [[spacetime]] ([[Minkowski space]]). For this article, the metric has ''mostly plus'' signature. The matter content is a real [[scalar field]] <math>S</math>, a real [[pseudoscalar]] field <math>P</math>, and a real ([[Majorana spinor|Majorana]]) [[spinor field]] <math>\psi</math>. 

This is a preliminary treatment in the sense that the theory is written in terms of familiar scalar and spinor fields which are functions of spacetime, without developing a theory of [[superspace]] or [[superfield]]s, which appear later in the article.

==== Free, massless theory ====

The Lagrangian of the free, massless Wess–Zumino model is
::<math> \mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}=-\frac{1}{2}(\partial S)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}(\partial P)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\bar{\psi} \partial\!\!\!/ \psi,</math>
where 
* <math>\partial \!\!\!/ = \gamma^\mu \partial_\mu</math>
* <math>\bar \psi = \psi^t C = \psi^\dagger i \gamma^0.</math>
The corresponding action is
::<math> I_{\text{kin}} = \int d^4x \mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}</math>.

==== Massive theory ====

Supersymmetry is preserved when adding a mass term of the form
::<math>\mathcal{L}_{\text{m}} = -\frac{1}{2}m^2 S^2 -\frac{1}{2}m^2 P^2 - \frac{1}{2}m\bar{\psi}\psi</math>

==== Interacting theory ====

Supersymmetry is preserved when adding an interaction term with coupling constant <math>\lambda</math>:
::<math>\mathcal{L}_{\text{int}} = -\lambda\left(\bar\psi(S-P\gamma_5)\psi + \frac{1}{2}\lambda(S^2 + P^2)^2 + mS(S^2 + P^2)\right).</math>

The full Wess–Zumino action is then given by putting these Lagrangians together:
{{Equation box 1
|title='''Wess–Zumino action (preliminary treatment)'''
|indent=:
|equation = <math>I_{\text{WZ}} = \int d^4x\ (\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{m}} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{int}}) </math>
|border
|border colour =#50C878
|background colour = #ECFCF4
}}

==== Alternative expression ====

There is an alternative way of organizing the fields. The real fields <math>S</math> and <math>P</math> are combined into a single ''complex'' scalar field <math>\phi := \frac{1}{2}(S + iP),</math> while the Majorana spinor is written in terms of two Weyl spinors: <math>\psi = (\chi^\alpha, \bar \chi_\dot\alpha)</math>. Defining the superpotential 
:<math>W(\phi):= \frac{1}{2}m\phi^2 + \frac{1}{3}\lambda \phi^3,</math>
the Wess–Zumino action can also be written (possibly after relabelling some constant factors)
{{Equation box 1
|title='''Wess–Zumino action (preliminary treatment, alternative expression)'''
|indent=:
|equation = <math>I_{\text{WZ}} = \int d^4x \left[\partial_\mu \phi^\dagger \partial^\mu \phi - i\chi\sigma^\mu \partial_\mu \bar\chi - \left|\frac{\partial W}{\partial\phi}\right|^2 - \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^2W}{\partial \phi^2}\chi\chi - \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^2W^\dagger}{\partial \phi^{\dagger 2}}\bar\chi\bar\chi\right] </math>
|border
|border colour =#50C878
|background colour = #ECFCF4
}}

Upon substituting in <math>W(\phi)</math>, one finds that this is a theory with a massive complex scalar <math>\phi</math> and a massive Majorana spinor <math>\psi</math> of the ''same'' mass. The interactions are a cubic and quartic <math>\phi</math> interaction, and a [[Yukawa interaction]] between <math>\phi</math> and <math>\psi</math>, which are all familiar interactions from courses in non-supersymmetric quantum field theory.

=== Using superspace and superfields ===

==== Superspace and superfield content ====

Superspace consists of the direct sum of Minkowski space with 'spin space', a four dimensional space with coordinates <math>(\theta_\alpha, \bar\theta^\dot\alpha)</math>, where <math>\alpha, \dot\alpha</math> are indices taking values in <math>1,2.</math> More formally, superspace is constructed as the space of right cosets of the Lorentz group in the [[Super-Poincaré algebra|super-Poincaré group]].

The fact there is only 4 'spin coordinates' means that this is a theory with what is known as <math>\mathcal{N} = 1</math> supersymmetry, corresponding to an algebra with a single [[supercharge]]. The <math>8 = 4 + 4</math> dimensional superspace is sometimes written <math>\mathbb{R}^{1,3|4}</math>, and called [[super Minkowski space]]. The 'spin coordinates' are so called not due to any relation to angular momentum, but because they are treated as [[Grassmann number|anti-commuting numbers]], a property typical of spinors in quantum field theory due to the [[spin statistics theorem]].

A superfield <math>\Phi</math> is then a function on superspace, <math>\Phi = \Phi(x, \theta, \bar\theta)</math>. 

Defining the supercovariant derivative
:<math>\bar D_\dot\alpha = \bar\partial_\dot\alpha - i(\bar\sigma^\mu)_{\dot\alpha\beta}\theta^\beta\partial_\mu,</math>
a '''chiral''' superfield satisfies <math>\bar D_\dot\alpha \Phi = 0.</math> The field content is then simply a single chiral superfield.

However, the chiral superfield ''contains''  fields, in the sense that it admits the expansion
:<math>\Phi(x, \theta, \bar\theta) = \phi(y) + \theta \chi(y) + \theta^2 F(y)</math>
with <math>y^\mu = x^\mu - i\theta\sigma^\mu \bar\theta.</math> Then <math>\phi</math> can be identified as a complex scalar, <math>\chi</math> is a [[Weyl spinor]] and <math>F</math> is an auxiliary complex scalar.

These fields admit a further relabelling, with <math>\phi = \frac{1}{2}(S + iP)</math> and <math>\psi^a = (\chi^\alpha, \bar\chi_{\dot\alpha}).</math> This allows recovery of the preliminary forms, after eliminating the non-dynamical <math>F</math> using its equation of motion.

==== Free, massless action ====

When written in terms of the chiral superfield <math>\Phi</math>, the action (for the free, massless Wess–Zumino model) takes on the simple form
:<math>\int d^4x d^2\theta d^2\bar\theta \,\, 2\bar\Phi \Phi</math>
where <math>\int d^2\theta, \int d^2\bar\theta</math> are [[Berezin integral|integrals over spinor dimensions]] of [[superspace]].

==== Superpotential ====

Masses and interactions are added through a '''superpotential'''. The Wess–Zumino superpotential is
:<math>W(\Phi) = m\Phi^2 + \frac{4}{3}\lambda\Phi^3.</math>
Since <math>W(\Phi)</math> is complex, to ensure the action is real its conjugate must also be added. 
The full Wess–Zumino action is written
{{Equation box 1
|title='''Wess–Zumino action'''
|indent=:
|equation = <math>I_{\text{WZ}} = \int d^4x \left[\int d^2\theta d^2\bar\theta \,\, \bar\Phi\Phi\right] + \left[\int d^2\theta W(\Phi) + \int d^2\bar\theta \bar W(\bar\Phi)\right]</math>
|border
|border colour =#50C878
|background colour = #ECFCF4
}}

== Supersymmetry of the action ==

=== Preliminary treatment ===

The action is invariant under the supersymmetry transformations, given in infinitesimal form by
::<math>\delta_{\epsilon} S=\bar{\epsilon} \psi</math>
::<math>\delta_{\epsilon} P =\bar{\epsilon} \gamma_{5} \psi</math>
::<math>\delta_{\epsilon} \psi = [\partial\!\!\!/ - m - \lambda (S+P\gamma_{5}) ] (S+P\gamma_{5})\epsilon</math>

where <math>\epsilon</math> is a Majorana spinor-valued transformation parameter and <math>\gamma_{5}</math> is the [[Chirality (physics)#Chiral theories|chirality operator]].

The alternative form is invariant under the transformation
::<math>\delta_\epsilon \phi = \sqrt 2 \epsilon \chi</math>
::<math>\delta_\epsilon \chi = \sqrt 2 i \sigma^\mu \bar\epsilon \partial_\mu \phi - \sqrt 2 \epsilon \frac{\partial W^\dagger}{\partial \phi^\dagger}</math>.

Without developing a theory of superspace transformations, these symmetries appear ad-hoc.

=== Superfield treatment ===

If the action can be written as
<math>S = \int d^4 x d^4 \theta K(x, \theta, \bar \theta)</math>
where <math>K</math> is a real superfield, that is, <math>K^\dagger = K</math>, then the action is invariant under supersymmetry.

Then the reality of <math>K = \bar\Phi \Phi</math> means it is invariant under supersymmetry.

== Extra classical symmetries ==

=== Superconformal symmetry ===
The ''massless'' Wess–Zumino model admits a larger set of symmetries, described at the algebra level by the [[superconformal algebra]]. As well as the Poincaré symmetry generators and the supersymmetry translation generators, this contains the conformal algebra as well as a conformal supersymmetry generator <math>S_\alpha</math>. 

The conformal symmetry is broken at the quantum level by trace and conformal anomalies, which break invariance under the conformal generators <math>D</math> for dilatations and <math>K_\mu</math> for [[special conformal transformation]]s respectively.

=== R-symmetry ===

The <math>\text{U}(1)</math> [[R-symmetry]] of <math>\mathcal{N} = 1</math> supersymmetry holds when the superpotential <math>W(\Phi)</math> is a monomial. This means either <math>W(\phi) = \frac{1}{2}m\phi^2</math>, so that the superfield <math>\Phi</math> is massive but free (non-interacting), or <math>W(\Phi) = \frac{1}{3}\lambda\phi^3</math> so the theory is massless but (possibly) interacting.

This is broken at the quantum level by anomalies.

== Action for multiple chiral superfields ==
The action generalizes straightforwardly to multiple chiral superfields <math>\Phi^i</math> with <math>i = 1, \cdots, N</math>. The most general [[renormalizable]] theory is
:<math>I = \int d^4 x \, d^4\theta \, K_{i\bar j}\Phi^i\Phi^{\dagger\bar j} + \int d^4 x \left[ \int d^2 \theta \, W(\Phi) + \text{h.c.} \right]</math>
where the superpotential is 
:<math>W(\Phi) = a_i\Phi^i + \frac{1}{2} m_{ij} \Phi^i \Phi^j + \frac{1}{3} \lambda_{ijk} \Phi^i \Phi^j \Phi^k</math>,
where implicit summation is used. 

By a change of coordinates, under which <math>\Phi^i</math> transforms under <math>\text{GL}(N, \mathbb{C})</math>, one can set <math>K_{i\bar j} = \delta_{i \bar j}</math> without loss of generality. With this choice, the expression <math>K = \delta_{i \bar j} \Phi^i \Phi^{\dagger \bar j}</math> is known as the canonical [[Kähler potential]]. There is residual freedom to make a unitary transformation in order to diagonalise the mass matrix <math>m_{ij}</math>.

When <math>N = 1</math>, if the multiplet is massive then the Weyl fermion has a Majorana mass. But for <math>N = 2,</math> the two Weyl fermions can have a Dirac mass, when the superpotential is taken to be
<math>W(\Phi, \tilde \Phi) = m\tilde\Phi\Phi.</math> This theory has a <math>\text{U}(1)</math> symmetry, where <math>\Phi, \tilde\Phi</math> rotate with opposite charges

=== Super QCD ===
{{See also | Super QCD}}

For general <math>N</math>, a superpotential of the form <math>W(\Phi_a, \tilde \Phi_a) = m\tilde\Phi_a\Phi_a</math> has a <math>\text{SU}(N)</math> symmetry when <math>\Phi_a, \tilde\Phi_a</math> rotate with opposite charges, that is under <math>U \in \text{SU}(N)</math>
:<math>\Phi_a \mapsto U_a{}^b\Phi_b</math>
:<math>\tilde \Phi_a \mapsto (U^{-1})_a{}^b\tilde\Phi_b </math>.

This symmetry can be gauged and coupled to [[N = 1 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory|supersymmetric Yang–Mills]] to form a supersymmetric analogue to [[quantum chromodynamics]], known as super QCD.

=== Supersymmetric sigma models ===
{{See also | non-linear sigma model}}

If renormalizability is not insisted upon, then there are two possible generalizations. The first of these is to consider more general superpotentials. The second is to consider <math>K</math> in the [[kinetic term]]
:<math>S = \int d^4x \, d^2\theta^2 \, d^2\bar\theta^2 K(\Phi, \bar\Phi)</math>
to be a real function <math>K = K(\Phi, \bar\Phi)</math> of <math>\Phi^i</math> and <math>\bar\Phi^\bar j</math>.

The action is invariant under transformations <math>K(\Phi, \Phi^\dagger) + \Lambda(\Phi) + \bar\Lambda(\bar\Phi)</math>: these are known as Kähler transformations.

Considering this theory gives an intersection of [[Kähler geometry]] with supersymmetric field theory.

By expanding the Kähler potential <math>K(\Phi, \bar\Phi)</math> in terms of derivatives of <math>K</math> and the constituent superfields of <math>\Phi, \bar\Phi</math>, and then eliminating the auxiliary fields <math>F, \bar F</math> using the equations of motion, the following expression is obtained:

:<math>S_K = \int d^4x \left[g_{ i \bar j } (\partial_\mu \phi^i \partial^\mu \bar \phi^\bar j) + g_{i \bar j}\frac{i}{2} (\nabla_\mu \psi^i \sigma^\mu \bar \psi ^\bar j - \psi^i \sigma^\mu \nabla_\mu \bar \psi^\bar j) + \frac{1}{4}R_{i\bar j k \bar l}(\psi^i \psi^k)(\bar \psi^\bar j \bar \psi^\bar l) \right]</math>
where
* <math>g_{i\bar j}</math> is the [[Kähler metric]]. It is invariant under Kähler transformations. If the kinetic term is positive definite, then <math>g_{i\bar j}</math> is invertible, allowing the inverse metric <math>g^{i\bar j}</math> to be defined.

* The [[Christoffel symbols]] (adapted for a Kähler metric) are <math>\Gamma^i{}_{jk} = g^{i\bar l}\partial_j g_{k \bar l}</math> and <math>\bar \Gamma^{\bar i} {} _{\bar j \bar k} = g^{l \bar i}\partial_{\bar j} g_{l \bar k}.</math>

* The [[covariant derivative]]s <math>\nabla_\mu \psi^i</math> and <math>\nabla_\mu \bar \psi^{\bar j}</math> are defined
:<math> \nabla_\mu \psi^i = \partial_\mu \psi^i + \Gamma ^i{}_{jk} \psi^j \partial_\mu \phi^k</math>
and 
:<math> \nabla_\mu \bar\psi^{\bar i} = \partial_\mu \psi^{\bar i} + \bar \Gamma ^{\bar i}{}_{\bar j \bar k} \bar \psi^{\bar j} \partial_\mu \bar \phi^{\bar k}</math>

* The [[Riemann curvature tensor]] (adapted for a Kähler metric) is defined <math>R_{i\bar j k\bar l} = g_{m \bar j} \partial_{\bar l} \Gamma^m{}_{ik} = \partial_k\partial_{\bar l} g_{i \bar j} - g^{m \bar n} (\partial_k g_{i \bar n}) (\partial_{\bar l}g_{m \bar j})</math>.

==== Adding a superpotential ====
A superpotential <math>W(\Phi)</math> can be added to form the more general action
:<math>S = S_K - \int d^4 x \left[g^{i \bar j} \partial_i W \partial_{\bar j} \bar W + \frac{1}{4}\psi^i \psi^j H_{ij}(W) + \frac{1}{4}\bar \psi^{\bar i} \bar \psi^{\bar j}H_{\bar i \bar j}(\bar W)\right]</math>
where the [[Hessian matrix | Hessian]]s of <math>W</math> are defined
:<math>H_{ij}(W) = \nabla_i\partial_j W = \partial_i \partial_j W - \Gamma^k{}_{ij} \partial_k W</math>
:<math>\bar H_{\bar i \bar j}(\bar W) = \nabla_{\bar i}\partial_{\bar j} \bar W = \partial_{\bar i} \partial_{\bar j} \bar W - \Gamma^{\bar k}{}_{\bar i \bar j} \partial_{\bar k} \bar W</math>.
